title: Fragments
tagline: An investment DAO solution with multichain fundraising, NFT to ERC-20 conversion, gasless voting and vault creation
description:
Feature descriptions based on our 3 personas; Investors, Delegates and Asset Owners.

The Investors can :
- Deposit any EVM-compatible token to invest in a vault 
- Track all their investments in a consolidated view
- Have an ERC20 token to represent their share in a vault
- Vote on proposals proportional to their share in a vault
- View all announcements regarding the DAO investments in one place
- Explore and invest in purchase orders with DAOs on the platform

The Delegate can:
- Set up a vault to collectively invest with their community
- Each vault can have a single or multiple purchase orders to invest in NFTs, tokens, and Defi pools.
- Make announcements and proposals that all investors can vote on according to their share in the vault

The Asset Owner can:
- Set up a vault to collectively invest with their community
- Start a purchase order to fractionalize their current NFT.
- Airdrop ERC-20 tokens to their investors to represent their share in the vault.
- Make announcements and proposals that all investors can vote on according to their share in the vault
how_its_made:
Web 3
Networks - Polygon and Ethereum
Token distribution - Polygon, help reduce the gas cost to distribute tokens
Voting and Proposals - Polygon, helped reduce the gas cost for voting so that we can bear the gas cost for the user
Safe Creation - Gnosis Safe
Storage - IPFS, helped in enabling NFT storage
NFT APIs - NFTPort, helped fetch the real-time price of the NFTs
Multichain bridge - Socket Tech, helped in making deposits easier from any chain and token
Libraries - ethers.js, web3.js, 

Frontend - next.js, Tailwind CSS

Backend 
node.js - run time environment
DynamoDB AWS - database to share data between L1 and L2
Lambda AWS - Authentication for fundraising completion, token airdrop and deploying Gnosis Safe across Ethereum, Polygon and other EVM chains
API gateway AWS - Adding security to our Lambda functions
